definitions.gloss: to write down; to note; to jot down
definitions.explanation: To record something in writing so as not to forget it.

examples.japanese: ⟦{電話番号|でんわばんごう}→電話番号：10159_denwabangou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{書|か}き{留|と}めた。
examples.english: I wrote down the phone number.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大事|だいじ}な→大事：01253_daiji⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦メモ→メモ：00274_memo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{書|か}き{留|と}めて⟦おこう→おく：01092_oku⟧。
examples.english: Let's jot down the important things in a memo.

examples.japanese: ⟦{会議|かいぎ}→会議：00710_kaigi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{内容|ないよう}→内容：01482_naiyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{詳|くわ}しく→詳しい：02483_kuwashii⟧{書|か}き{留|と}める。
examples.english: I'll note down the meeting contents in detail.

examples.japanese: ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}き→聞く：00483_kiku⟧⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧、⟦{大事|だいじ}な→大事：01253_daiji⟧⟦ところ→所：01137_tokoro⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{書|か}き{留|と}めた。
examples.english: I jotted down the important points while listening to the teacher.

examples.japanese: ⟦{旅行|りょこう}→旅行：00748_ryokou⟧⟦{先|さき}→先：02883_saki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{出会|であ}った→出会う：02298_deau⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{名前|なまえ}→名前：02234_namae⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{住所|じゅうしょ}→住所：01430_juusho⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{書|か}き{留|と}めて⟦おいた→おく：01092_oku⟧⟦おかげ→おかげ：01362_okage⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{後|あと}→後：09580_ato⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{手紙|てがみ}→手紙：00675_tegami⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧⟦こと→こと：01164_koto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できた→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: Thanks to having written down the names and addresses of people I met during my trip, I was able to send them letters afterward.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: ⟦{他動詞|たどうし}→他動詞：10418_tadoushi⟧ (transitive), with no intransitive pair. What gets written down is marked with ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧; where it is written goes with ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- 〜⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{書|か}き{留|と}める: write ~ down
- ⟦{手帳|てちょう}→手帳：04537_techou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{書|か}き{留|と}める: write it down in a planner
- {書|か}き{留|と}めて⟦おく→おく：01092_oku⟧: write it down now so it is there later. This is the commonest shape of the verb, because the point of writing something down is almost always the later use.

FORMATION: ⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧ (write) + ⟦{留|と}める→止める：00678_tomeru⟧ (fasten, hold in place). The second half is what separates it from plain ⟦{書|か}く→書く：00477_kaku⟧: it is writing that pins information down so it will not be lost.

WATCH OUT: the noun ⟦{書留|かきとめ}→書留：00150_kakitome⟧, written with the same two characters but no okurigana, is registered mail. It is a different word, not a form of this verb.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦メモする→メモする：25501_memosuru⟧ is the casual everyday equivalent, and what most people actually say.
- ⟦{記録|きろく}→記録：02490_kiroku⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ is to record systematically, for data or an official account, not for a personal reminder.
- ⟦{控|ひか}える→控える：10054_hikaeru⟧ overlaps for jotting down numbers and details to keep on hand; it also has an unrelated sense of refraining.

REGISTER: neutral but slightly careful and bookish. In casual speech ⟦メモする→メモする：25501_memosuru⟧ or ⟦{書|か}いて→書く：00477_kaku⟧⟦おく→おく：01092_oku⟧ is more likely.
